usage_note: be crazy about + noun / -ing: 'She is crazy about football.' Informal; used after be, get or go.

relations.note: Liking something a lot, a little less strong.
Liking something in a calm, warm way.
No longer enjoying something because you have had too much of it.

context.text: My little brother is crazy about cars. He knows every car on the streets of Tashkent and talks about them all day.

reviewer_note: Informal register marked; crazy (adj) alone has a different meaning (mad).

forms.definition: a person who breaks the law
forms.example: The criminal was sent to prison for five years.

syn.note: A more formal word, often used by the police and courts.
Someone who does not obey the law.
A dishonest person, often one who steals.
One type of law-breaker: a person who steals.

forms.definition: an action that is against the law
forms.example: Stealing a phone is a crime.

syn.note: A formal word for an illegal act. American spelling: offense.
Bad or illegal behaviour in general.

forms.note: The headword is made from this noun: crime + -al.

forms.definition: to make an action illegal by law
forms.example: Some countries criminalize selling fake medicine.

syn.note: To make something illegal.
To say officially that something is not allowed.

ant.note: To make something allowed by law.
To stop an action being illegal.

forms.definition: connected with breaking the law
forms.example: The police are looking into criminal activity in the area.

syn.note: Not allowed by law; the easiest word.
A formal word for illegal.

ant.note: Allowed by law.
Allowed by law; formal.

forms.definition: in a way that breaks the law
forms.example: He was charged with acting criminally.

syn.note: Against the law.

ant.note: In a way the law allows.

people.definition: an expert who studies why people break the law
people.example: A criminologist spoke on the news about car theft.

people.definition: the study of law-breaking and law-breakers
people.example: She is studying criminology at university.

context.text: Last night the police caught a criminal near Chorsu Bazaar. He stole bags from tourists, and that is a serious crime.

reviewer_note: Rule 6: person-noun headword stays main in the noun slot; crime as extra (source noun).

forms.definition: words that say what is bad or wrong about something
forms.example: The new law got a lot of criticism.

syn.note: A feeling or sign that you do not like something.
Saying you are unhappy about something.
Saying someone is responsible for something bad.

ant.note: Words that say something is good.
Thinking something is good or right.

forms.definition: to say what you think is bad about someone or something
forms.example: Please do not criticize my cooking!

syn.note: Stronger: to say something is very wrong.
To say someone is responsible for something bad.
To criticize very strongly, often in public.

ant.note: To say good things about someone.
To say something nice about someone.

forms.definition: saying that someone or something is bad or wrong
forms.example: My father was critical of my plan.
forms.note: critical also means 'very important' (a critical moment).

syn.note: Showing you do not like something.
Seeing only the bad side.

ant.note: Showing you think something is good.
Saying nice things.

forms.definition: in a way that points out faults
forms.example: The teacher spoke critically about our homework.

syn.note: In a way that shows you do not like something.

ant.note: In a way that shows you like something.

people.definition: a person who writes opinions about films, books or art
people.example: The film critic loved the new Uzbek movie.

context.text: My teacher's criticism helped me a lot. She criticized my essay, but she also showed me how to make it better.

reviewer_note: critical has a second meaning (very important); noted on the entry.

particle_note: Separable: cross out the word / cross the word out; with a pronoun only cross it out.

relations.note: The same action, a little more formal.
To remove words, often on a computer.
To remove writing completely, for example with a rubber.

context.text: I made a mistake in my answer, so I crossed out the wrong word. Then I wrote the right one above it.

reviewer_note: No true antonym, so none listed.

forms.definition: a holiday on a big ship that visits several places
forms.example: They went on a cruise around the Greek islands.

syn.note: A long journey by sea; not always a holiday.
Any short journey for fun or work.

forms.definition: to travel on a ship for a holiday
forms.example: We cruised along the coast for a week.

syn.note: To travel by boat or ship.

people.definition: a large motor boat with rooms for sleeping
people.example: They rented a cruiser for the weekend.

context.text: My grandparents went on a cruise last summer. They cruised from Italy to Spain and loved every day.

reviewer_note: cruiser also means a warship and a US police car; the boat sense is kept.

forms.definition: a strong, short feeling of love for someone
forms.example: She has a crush on a boy in her class.
forms.note: Belongs to crush = a short love feeling, not pressing something.

forms.definition: to press something hard so that it breaks or loses its shape
forms.example: Do not crush the eggs in the shopping bag.

syn.note: To press something until it is flat or soft.
To break something into many pieces, often with noise.
To push hard on something; not always breaking it.

forms.definition: pressed into very small pieces
forms.example: Add some crushed garlic to the soup.

syn.note: Pressed flat or out of shape.
Made into powder, like coffee or pepper.

forms.definition: very bad and making you lose hope
forms.example: The team suffered a crushing defeat.
forms.note: Belongs to crush = defeat completely, not pressing something.
crushingly (crushingly boring) exists but is rare and belongs to the 'very bad' meaning.

people.definition: a machine or tool that breaks things into small pieces
people.example: Use the garlic crusher in the drawer.

context.text: My mother told me not to crush the bread in my bag. At home she put crushed garlic and tomatoes in the soup.

reviewer_note: Noun crush (love) and crushing (defeat) kept as other_meaning.

forms.definition: a medicine or treatment that makes an ill person well
forms.example: There is still no cure for the common cold.

syn.note: Something that makes an illness better.
Medical care; it may not make you fully well.
A drug you take when you are ill.

forms.definition: to make a sick person healthy again
forms.example: This medicine can cure the infection in a week.

syn.note: To make a person or a wound healthy again.
To give medical care; the person may not get fully well.

forms.definition: possible to make healthy again with treatment
forms.example: Luckily, her illness is curable.

syn.note: Doctors can help with it.

ant.note: Impossible to make better.

context.text: The doctor said my grandfather's illness is curable. With the right medicine, she can cure it in a month.

reviewer_note: 2 rows merged (same meaning, B1). curator shares an old Latin root but is not made from cure. cure = preserve meat with salt not shown.

forms.definition: a piece of hair that has a round, twisted shape
forms.example: The baby has soft blonde curls.

syn.note: A long, hanging piece of twisted hair.
A gentle bend in hair, not a full round shape.
A round shape like a spring; used for rope and wire too.

forms.definition: to make something form a round, twisted shape
forms.example: She curls her hair before parties.

syn.note: To turn something round and round.
To turn something over and over into a round shape.
To change something from straight to not straight.

ant.note: To make something straight.

forms.definition: having many round, twisted shapes
forms.example: Malika has long curly hair.

syn.note: With gentle bends, not tight round shapes.

ant.note: Not bent at all.

forms.definition: bent into a round shape
forms.example: The cat lay curled on the sofa.

syn.note: Turned round and round.

ant.note: Not bent at all.

people.definition: a small tube you put in hair to give it round shapes
people.example: My aunt sleeps with curlers in her hair.

context.text: Malika was born with curly hair. Her sister has straight hair, so she curls it every morning with a hot brush.

reviewer_note: curl up (sit with legs bent) is a phrasal verb and not shown here.

forms.definition: a strong movement of water, air or electricity
forms.example: The river has a very strong current.
forms.note: Belongs to current = a flow of water or electricity, not 'happening now'.

forms.definition: the money used in a country
forms.example: The currency of Uzbekistan is the sum.
forms.note: Belongs to current in its old meaning 'moving around'; money that is in use.

forms.definition: happening or true at this time
forms.example: What is your current address?

syn.note: Existing now; a little formal before a noun.
There now, already in place.
Of the present time, often new and up to date.

ant.note: In the past, but not now.
Happening before this one.
Belonging to a time before now.

forms.definition: at the present time
forms.example: I am currently looking for a new job.

syn.note: The easiest word for this time.
Mainly American in this meaning; in British English it often means 'soon'.

ant.note: In the past, but not now.
Before now.

context.text: My current job is in the centre of Tashkent. I am currently looking for a flat closer to the office.

reviewer_note: False friends for Russian speakers: current is not 'текущий' in the water sense; noun current and currency kept as other_meaning.

forms.definition: magic words that wish something bad on someone
forms.example: The witch put a curse on the prince.

syn.note: Bad luck that someone or something seems to bring.
Magic words; a spell can be good or bad.

ant.note: A wish or prayer for something good.

forms.definition: to use magic words to make bad things happen to someone
forms.example: In the story, an old woman cursed the king.
forms.note: curse also means 'to swear, say rude words'.

syn.note: To put bad magic on someone; mainly American.
To bring bad luck.

ant.note: To ask God or magic to protect someone.

forms.definition: having bad magic on it
forms.example: Nobody wanted to live in the cursed house.

syn.note: Having bad luck all the time.
Sure to end badly.

ant.note: Protected by God or good luck.

context.text: In the old tale, a witch put a curse on the king. After that, nobody dared to enter the cursed castle for a hundred years.

reviewer_note: curse = swear (rude words) noted on the verb.
